name: Malachi
whenBasis: The book is undated. The temple is standing and sacrifices offered (Malachi 1:7–10), and a governor rules (1:8), so it falls in the Persian period after 515 BC. Its concerns, mixed marriages and withheld tithes, are also Nehemiah's.
summary: The prophet whose book closes the twelve. In a series of disputes the people ask how the LORD has loved them, how they have despised His name, how they rob Him. He rebukes priests who offer blind and lame animals, men who break faith with the wives of their youth, and a people who withhold tithes. He foretells the messenger who will prepare the way, and Elijah sent before the great day of the LORD.
body: “Try offering them to your governor!” he says of the sick animals brought to the altar. He calls the people to bring the full tithe into the storehouse and see if the LORD will not open the windows of heaven.
The gospels read his messenger and his Elijah of John the Baptist.

later.text: Malachi means “my messenger,” and it may be a title rather than a name; the Greek translation of 1:1 reads “by the hand of his messenger.”
One rabbi in the Talmud says Malachi was Mordecai, another that he was Ezra; the Targum names him Ezra the scribe.
